title: European Authors Day celebrations open a month dedicated to reading and European literature
content:
The initiative promotes European literature and encourages interest in reading, particularly among younger generations. 2026’s theme, friendship and togetherness, invites participants to connect offline by sharing books, conversations and ideas.

In 2025, schools, bookshops, libraries and other organisations in 34 countries hosted over 6 500 events and reading activities, including meetings with European authors, bringing together over 300 000 participants.

In 2026, almost 40 countries are expected to take part in the celebrations. Reading activities in local venues will create opportunities for authors and readers to meet. Organisations interested in taking part are invited to hold their own reading events.

From 11 November to 12 December, European Authors Day 2026 will celebrate reading and European literature under the hashtag #ReadForReal.

  • Find European Authors Day events near you on the #ReadForReal 2026 event map (external link)

    Link to the ReadForReal website.

    • Link to the ReadForReal website.

    One of the highlights of the 2026 edition will be the European Authors Day Tour, through which 35 authors will be traveling to meet readers across Europe.

title: EUmies Awards Young Talent 2027 – call for nominations open
content:
Funded by Creative Europe, the EUmies Awards Young Talent 2027 supports the talent of recently graduated architects, urban planners and landscape architects who will contribute to transforming our built environment in the future.

The awards are open to graduation projects completed and approved in architecture, landscape architecture and urban planning schools from countries participating in the Creative Europe programme, developed during 2025 and 2026, subject to the eligibility conditions established in the official rules.

  • 5 November 2026 – Call for nominations opens
  • 20 January 2027 – Deadline for nominations
  • April 2027 – Announcement of shortlisted projects
    The shortlisted projects will be announced at the EUmies Awards 2026 exhibition in Vilnius in the context of the Lithuanian Presidency of the Council of the European Union.
  • May 2027 – Announcement of finalists
  • June 2027 – Announcement of winners
    The winners will be announced during the EUmies Awards Days.

    • All nominated projects will be published online and become part of the EUmies Awards archive, recognising their authors and the schools that nominated them.

title: Calling Europe’s artists: tell us about your work!
content:
Coinciding with the first anniversary of the adoption of the Culture Compass for Europe, European Commissioner for Intergenerational Fairness, Youth, Culture and Sport, Glenn Micallef announced the publication of a new EU Artists’ Survey.

The survey takes just five minutes to complete and is available in all 24 official EU languages on the following topics:

  • pressures on their freedom to create
  • the conditions they work in
  • the impact of generative AI on their practice

    • The survey is open until Friday 15 January 2027. The survey results will help build the evidence base for cultural policy in Europe and will feed into a new report on the state of culture in the EU due in 2027, with a specific emphasis on artistic freedom.

    The European Commission published a new EU Artists Survey to gather information on artists’ experiences of artistic freedom and their working conditions, including the impact of generative AI.

  • Take the EU Artists’ Survey (external link)

title: Aalborg and Elsinore shortlisted for the European Capital of Culture 2032 in Denmark
content:
A panel of independent experts recommended Aalborg and Elsinore as the shortlisted cities at an announcement ceremony held on 12 November 2026 in the Ministry of Culture in Copenhagen.

Denmark invited applications on 1st December 2025. Two cities, Aalborg and Elsinore, submitted applications by the deadline of 5 October 2026.

Once the relevant Danish authorities endorse the panel's recommendation, the pre-selected cities will have until the summer of 2027 to complete their applications. The selection panel will then meet again in Copenhagen in September 2027 to recommend the Danish city to become European Capital of Culture in 2032.

Aalborg focusses on people, places, communities in transition and the power of art and culture to create belonging, forge bonds, show the way and open to the new. Art and culture should be the “engine for change” and urban regeneration in a time of social uncertainty, climate challenges and democratic pressures.

Aalborg Municipality is applying to become European Capital of Culture alongside other municipalities in North Jutland and Sermersooq Municipality in Greenland. They call their partnership Aalborg & Around.

title: Commissioner Micallef announces EU Culture Dialogue Community
content:
On 12 November 2026, Glenn Micallef European Commissioner for Intergenerational Fairness, Youth, Culture and Sport, held the first EU Culture Dialogue Annual Meeting. The event marks the first anniversary of the adoption of the Culture Compass for Europe.

At the meeting, Commissioner Micallef introduced the EU Culture Dialogue Community. The Commissioner is inviting organisations in the cultural and creative sectors to become part of a community of stakeholders that will be informed and consulted on developments in EU cultural policy and forthcoming relevant initiatives.

The EU Culture Dialogue Community is a new way for the cultural and creative sectors to help shape European cultural policy.

  • Register to become part of the EU Culture Dialogue Community (external link)

    • Representatives of Europe’s cultural and creative sectors spent the day discussing with Commissioner Micallef key actions of the Culture Compass for Europe for 2027, including an EU Artists’ Charter, an AI strategy for the cultural and creative sectors, and a new report on the state of culture in the EU, with a specific emphasis on artistic freedom.

title: EU Culture Dialogue
content:
The EU Culture Dialogue brings together the European Commission and Europe's cultural and creative sectors to exchange views, share experiences and help shape EU cultural policy.

Launched by European Commissioner for Intergenerational Fairness, Youth, Culture and Sport Glenn Micallef on 12 November 2026, the Dialogue supports the implementation of the Culture Compass for Europe.

Share your experiences of working in the cultural and creative sectors, including your working conditions, artistic freedom and the impact of artificial intelligence on your work.

The survey is available in all official EU languages and will be conducted annually. Your responses will help inform the annual State of Culture in the EU report.

Register to receive updates on EU cultural policy, contribute to consultations and workshops throughout the year, and help identify priorities for future EU Culture Dialogue meetings.

Participation in individual events is subject to availability. Registration does not guarantee an invitation.

Link to EU Survey.

title: Music Moves Europe Awards 2027 nominees announced
content:

  • TeddyBear, Belgium
  • Ida The Young, Czech Republic
  • panicbaby, Germany
  • Ángeles Toledano, Spain
  • Vilma Jää, Finland
  • Jersey, France
  • DA TI, Georgia
  • Alkyone, Greece
  • Palo Canto, Hungary
  • MOIO, Ireland
  • dóttir.x, Iceland
  • TÄRA, Italy
  • Nusantara Beat, Netherlands
  • Petra, Slovakia
  • Olga Myko, Sweden

    • The 15 nominees for the Music Moves Europe Awards 2027 are here. Music fans are invited to vote for their favourite artist.

    An international jury will select five MME Award winners and one Grand Jury Prize winner. The winners will be announced on 14 January 2027 in Groningen, the Netherlands, during Eurosonic Noorderslag (ESNS).

    Each MME Award winner will receive €10 000. The Grand Jury Prize winner will also receive a €5 000 green touring voucher. The Public Choice Award winner will receive €5 000 and the opportunity to record a Spotify Single at Spotify’s studio in Stockholm.

title: Creative Europe opens 2027 call for literary translation and promotion
content:
The call ‘circulation of European literary works’ supports the translation, publication, distribution and promotion of European literature, including novels, poetry, comics and plays, with a focus on works written in less widely translated languages.

Promoting reading and helping readers discover the diversity of languages and cultures reflected in European literature are also key objectives.

Publishers, booksellers and libraries are encouraged to work together to strengthen the book sector’s competitiveness. Ensuring fair pay and good working conditions for literary translators is also a priority.

Organisations in the publishing and book sector based in an eligible country can apply individually or as a group of two or more partners.

Each project must include a minimum of five eligible literary works, supported by a strong publishing strategy and a distribution plan.

The authors must be nationals or residents of an eligible country or be recognised as part of Europe’s literary heritage.

An online information session will take place on 17 November 2026 from 14:00 to 16:00.

title: Jury announces the finalist projects of the first edition of the Simone Veil Prize
content:
The international jury of independent experts announced the 25 finalist projects for the first edition of the Simone Veil prize. The jury recognised the finalists as high-quality projects that engage with Jewish cultural heritage to promote dialogue, inclusion, and a deeper understanding of Europe’s shared history.

  • DrawnTogether: A Children’s Picture Book Exhibition at Bergen-Belsen Memorial, Germany
  • “Le Vite” (“The Lives”): Reconnecting Lives through Archival Heritage, Italy
  • The Thinking Heart of the Barracks, Lithuania
  • The Fashion System. Clothes in strategies of violence and survival tactics in Łódź Ghetto, Poland
  • Where Silence Speaks: Transforming a Forgotten Jewish Cemetery into a Place of Learning, Dialogue and Shared European Memory, Slovakia
  • Eden, Austria
  • Murals, France
  • The Transplants, France
  • A Public Service: Remembering to Forget, Romania
  • In the Footsteps of Hidden Children Memorial - 2025 edition, Slovakia
  • Walls that Remember, Lithuania
  • Het Joods Manifest – The Jewish Manifesto, the Netherlands
  • From Silence to Living Heritage: A Grassroots Revival of Jewish Heritage in Europe's Borderlands, Slovenia
  • Georg Riedel’s Yiddishland, Sweden
  • J-Art Without Borders, Ukraine

title: Circulation of European literary works
content:
This action will support projects that translate, publish, distribute and promote European literary works written by authors linked to an eligible Creative Europe country by their nationality or place of residence, or recognised as belonging to the European literary heritage.

The action is expected to support around 40 projects, implemented either by a single entity (mono-beneficiary) or by a consortium of organisations (multi-beneficiary).

Along with activities related to literary works, activities that facilitate collaboration between different actors in the book and publishing value chain, such as authors, translators, publishers, distributors, booksellers, libraries, literary events and festivals, can also be funded.
